title: "David C. Francis"

::: {.eyebrow}
Senior Economist · World Bank, DEC Enterprise Analysis Unit
:::

::: {.lede}
I work on two things that turn out to be the same thing: measuring firms and
labor markets well, and using that measurement to identify how households and
firms respond when conditions change.
:::

I am a Senior Economist in the World Bank's DEC Enterprise Analysis Unit, where
I have worked since 2010. Much of my job is building data — I coordinate the
Informal Sector Enterprise Survey across 15 countries, have served as Task Team
Leader for Enterprise Surveys in roughly 60 economies, and advise on firm-level
question design for Business Ready (B-READY).

My research runs alongside that. Recent published work covers firm-level
political influence across 41 countries, the gendered labor allocation response
of agricultural households to herder-related violence, transactional governance
structures, and productivity and firm exit in developing countries. Current
projects use quasi-experimental designs to study labor supply responses to
pension reform in Argentina, sudden household deaths in South Africa, and
repeated drought in Mexico.

I am completing a Ph.D. in Public Policy and Administration at George Washington
University, concentrating in program evaluation. Before the World Bank I was a
Research Specialist at Princeton's Niehaus Center on Globalization and
Governance.
